findings.summary: CODEX-02-B at 606e8c5 implements the local synthetic adult verification/recovery slice within DECISION-039 / APPROVAL-006 (exact spec blob ee6381b2, track d77c78ce) and architecture v1.2 WM-02 VerifyAdult / ADR-E01/E02/E05: a real-PGlite transactional service storing only hashes, an Origin/Host/cookie-guarded loopback HTTP server, and a dev-gated UI. The browser correction is narrow. It exempts only the exact `user-agent` and `sec-fetch-user` header names and lets unrelated well-formed cookies coexist without granting authority. There are regression tests for both, and identity/forwarded/bearer/X-User-Id rejections still hold. All three acceptance criteria are covered: scope binding for new join, known join and recovery; generic invalid_link for invalid/expired/replayed codes, with check_inbox for unknown/disabled/throttled requests; and persistent cooldown/global budgets, no logging and capture-only delivery. The evidence is controller test/build/card-check output on the reviewed tree (60/60 pass, protected adult probe PASS) and a native CUA pass pinned to matching source blobs. Dependencies 01-B/01-C/00-C are recorded as done. The remaining issues are minor: stale text in the report, a passive cross-tab logout in the UI, and a timing/fault side channel that matters for production. Provider, identity-policy, consent, sending and admission gates stay open and are correctly not claimed.

findings.title: REPORT.md evidence is stale and self-contradictory for the reviewed commit
findings.problem: The card's completion record requires exact revisions and checks. The report still has the drafting-time table saying 'NOT YET RUN BY THIS AGENT' / 'Pending; no verdict claimed'. It also leaks an internal prompt instruction ('Return complete replacement contents...'). Its recorded controller output (02:45Z) is for eeba25e, before the 606e8c5 correction, and its last section says all native scenarios must be rerun and no review has happened. The actual 606e8c5 test/build/card-check results and the CUA pass (blobs cd8486a/1b5e2c4/50eb57a...) exist only in controller artifacts. As written, the merged report would not identify the accepted revision or its evidence.
findings.fix_check: At acceptance, the report (or the controller's acceptance record) names commit 606e8c5, links its actual test/build/card-check output and the CUA JSON/trace SHA-256, and marks the earlier pending table and the 'rerun required' note as superseded.

findings.title: Stale signed-out tab revokes a newer session on passive focus
findings.problem: After an explicit sign-out, suppressRestore stays true in that tab, and every focus, pageshow or visibility revalidation then POSTs /adult/logout. If the adult later verifies or recovers in another tab, which shares the Path=/adult cookie, just returning to the old tab revokes the new session. The verified tab then drops to signed-out on its next 15-second poll. This fails closed, so it is not a security issue, but it is a confusing failure in the recover-access journey. Passive checks should not change server state.
findings.fix_check: Passive revalidation while suppressed only clears local identity and does not call logout. Or: a two-tab test (sign out in A, verify in B, focus A) confirms B stays restricted.

findings.title: Eligible vs ineligible requests differ in timing and in delivery-fault status
findings.problem: Bodies are identical, but eligible requests (known account, or unknown join) await the delivery callback and a second transaction. Unknown recovery, disabled and throttled requests return right after the first transaction. If delivery faults, only eligible requests return 503, while ineligible ones always return check_inbox. With in-process capture this is a small local signal. The architecture requires that the verification challenge not enumerate households, and a real provider adapter would widen both channels. This is acceptable to defer under the open provider/G-E03 gates, but the contract does not record it.
findings.fix_check: ADULT_ACCESS_CONTRACT.md records the timing/fault enumeration channel as an open production obligation for the provider adapter (for example, dispatch asynchronously after a uniform response). Or the service equalizes the response path.

findings.title: Strict cookie grammar can block the page on shared 127.0.0.1 cookies
findings.problem: Browser cookies for 127.0.0.1 are not isolated by port. Any other local dev app that sets a quoted or comma-containing cookie value will cause a 400 even on the trusted asset/entry path. The contract documents this fail-closed behaviour, and the CUA did not hit it, but it is a likely local interoperability surprise.
findings.fix_check: Either document the remedy (clear 127.0.0.1 cookies) in the contract or UI support text, or relax asset-path parsing to ignore unparseable non-adult cookies while keeping /adult APIs strict.

findings.title: Status ledger records blocked state against an unrelated main commit
findings.problem: The committed status file says state 'blocked' with result_commit 16bd411, the PR #15 merge on main, not this candidate. This is controller-owned, but if merged unchanged it misstates the task's state.
findings.fix_check: The controller updates state, result_commit and accepted fields to the accepted candidate when it records delegated acceptance.
